items.questionAndWhy: How well do empirical studies substantiate claims that AI use harms cognition, relationships, information integrity or autonomy?
items.whatTheyDid: Summerfield and colleagues reviewed model evaluations, user studies, consumer conversation records and agent simulations across eight domains of possible human impact.
items.whatTheyFound: The review finds limited evidence for the strongest harm narratives, while emphasizing that the evidence base is immature. Designs differ in outcomes and populations; absence of strong evidence is not evidence of safety.
items.whatItMeans: PSYWERX can distinguish measured human outcomes from model-only tests and prioritize longitudinal or experimental studies of independent reasoning, dependence and information quality. This review does not establish a single effect size.
items.streamTitle: AI impact review finds limited evidence for strongest claims of harm
items.streamSummary: A peer-reviewed review of eight AI impact domains finds limited support for the strongest harm claims, with substantial unresolved uncertainty and heterogeneous evidence.
items.attribution: Summerfield, Anselmetti, Avin et al. — Nature Human Behaviour (review; November 24, 2026)

items.questionAndWhy: Does a poorly performing reverse-worded happiness item reflect an intrinsically weak measure or heterogeneous response patterns?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers used latent profile analysis of four-item Subjective Happiness Scale responses from 303 Chilean adults.
items.whatTheyFound: Five profiles emerged; one comprising 10.56% of respondents gave discordant responses to the reverse-worded item. Excluding that group increased the item loading and correlations, with modest reliability gains. The analysis is observational and does not identify why participants responded differently.
items.whatItMeans: PSYWERX survey designers can inspect person-level response patterns before deleting reverse-worded items or treating composite scores as comparable. Replication across constructs and languages is needed.
items.streamTitle: Reverse-worded survey item behaved differently in a subgroup
items.streamSummary: A 303-person Chilean psychometric study identified a subgroup with discordant reverse-item responses; excluding it improved item performance. The cause of the wording pattern remains unknown.
items.attribution: Clavijo-García, Vargas-Garrido, Rosales-Miranda et al. — Scientific Reports (psychometric study; November 23, 2026)

items.questionAndWhy: What do people responsible for countering disinformation believe drives the problem, and what constraints limit their work?
items.whatTheyDid: Darcy and Altay surveyed 106 French practitioners across government, military, regulators, media and civil society, and descriptively compared views with a separate academic survey.
items.whatTheyFound: Respondents emphasized production and platform amplification; they reported weak coordination, limited resources and concern about censorship accusations. Few directly read research despite trusting it; only 13% believed institutions could contain the threat. These are practitioner perceptions, not objective effectiveness measures; the academic comparison used different instruments and timing.
items.whatItMeans: PSYWERX practitioner education could evaluate whether shared indicators and accessible research summaries address reported organizational barriers. The survey does not establish which counter-disinformation interventions work.
items.streamTitle: French counter-disinformation practitioners reported coordination and evidence-use barriers
items.streamSummary: A survey of 106 French practitioners found an upstream diagnosis of disinformation alongside coordination and research-access barriers. Self-reported assessments do not measure intervention effectiveness.
items.attribution: Darcy and Altay — Harvard Kennedy School Misinformation Review (practitioner survey; October 22, 2026)

items.questionAndWhy: How can allied units develop the organizational and communications compatibility needed for coordinated activity?
items.whatTheyDid: The Estonian Defence Forces announced the November 23–December 11 Pikne exercise involving Estonian, French and British forces and the Estonian Defence League.
items.whatTheyFound: The official announcement identifies cooperation and command-and-communications compatibility as training objectives. It describes an exercise beginning November 23, not completed performance or independently measured improvements.
items.whatItMeans: PSYWERX exercise assessment can distinguish technical message exchange from shared understanding and coordination, measuring each with predefined non-sensitive evaluation criteria. No exercise effect has yet been demonstrated in this announcement.
items.streamTitle: Estonian multinational exercise emphasizes command and communications interoperability
items.streamSummary: Estonia announced a multinational exercise emphasizing command and communications compatibility; these are stated readiness objectives, not measured interoperability gains.
items.attribution: Estonian Defence Forces — Exercise Pikne 2026 announcement (November 23, 2026)

items.questionAndWhy: Do consumer AI products that make accurate point predictions also provide trustworthy prediction intervals?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers tested six consumer LLM products in 142 sessions during February–March 2026, including next-day forecasts for seven financial, weather, sports and cryptocurrency variables.
items.whatTheyFound: Nominal 90% interval coverage ranged from 22.9% to 80.0% across products. One model ranked relatively well on point error but covered only 11 of 37 outcomes (29.7%); widening its intervals retrospectively improved coverage. Small samples and in-sample adjustments limit conclusions, and data freshness may explain some errors.
items.whatItMeans: PSYWERX forecast evaluation should score point accuracy, interval coverage and input timestamps separately. A model's stated confidence is not a calibrated probability of an operational outcome.
items.streamTitle: Accurate AI point forecasts did not guarantee calibrated uncertainty
items.streamSummary: Six consumer AI products showed substantial undercoverage of nominal 90% prediction intervals, even when point estimates were relatively accurate. The descriptive benchmark is small and version-specific.
items.attribution: Pandit, Pandit and Pandit — Scientific Reports (forecast benchmark; November 24, 2026)

items.questionAndWhy: Can passing evidence metadata with a claim reduce unsupported changes as multiple AI agents summarize it?
items.whatTheyDid: Cao and Dou passed FEVER claims labeled insufficiently supported through five-stage pipelines using five open-weight models, comparing text-only and provenance-aware transmissions without introducing new evidence.
items.whatTheyFound: At stage five, semantic equivalence in same-model pipelines rose from 62.67% to 96.95% with provenance metadata; in the fixed mixed-model sequence it rose from 31.33% to 95.73%. Metadata preservation was imperfect. This preprint tests claim fidelity, not truth verification, and model order was confounded in the mixed sequence.
items.whatItMeans: PSYWERX research agents could carry claim IDs, source passages, evidence status and revision history through every handoff. Independent source checks remain necessary; faithful transmission can preserve an unsupported claim.
items.streamTitle: Provenance records reduced claim drift across AI handoffs
items.streamSummary: A five-stage AI benchmark found structured provenance greatly reduced claim drift and unsupported additions. The approach preserves evidence status rather than verifying truth.

items.questionAndWhy: Which format best distinguishes forecaster skill when outcomes are continuous quantities?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers compared fixed-probability quantile estimates with probabilities assigned to fixed outcome bins, using simulation and five forecasting waves from 1,194 participants on 36 real-world questions.
items.whatTheyFound: Quantile-format scores showed higher internal consistency and lower measurement error; tolerable reliability was possible with about six questions versus more than twice as many for the alternative. Quantile answers took effort and sometimes violated monotonicity, but coherence improved with practice. Findings concern continuous outcomes, not every forecasting task.
items.whatItMeans: PSYWERX expert elicitation could ask for outcome quantiles, check ordering and score forecasts against later observations before weighting experts by performance. The study does not establish reliable causal intervention forecasts.
items.streamTitle: Quantile elicitation improved reliability of forecaster skill measurement
items.streamSummary: Simulation and longitudinal forecasts from 1,194 participants found quantile elicitation more efficient for measuring forecaster skill, though coherence and effort remained challenges.
items.attribution: Zhu, Budescu, Petrov, Karger and Himmelstein — Judgment and Decision Making (simulation and longitudinal survey; October 14, 2026)

items.questionAndWhy: Can synchronized measurements support analysis of attention and actual behavior in a real-world task?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers released urban manual-driving recordings with wearable eye tracking, heart rate, GPS, vehicle controls, questionnaires and within-person music/no-music conditions.
items.whatTheyFound: The open dataset supports time-linked analysis of gaze and control actions. Quality checks are documented, but sensors lacked a shared hardware clock and residual timing error cannot be quantified; video is withheld for consent reasons. The descriptor does not demonstrate a music effect.
items.whatItMeans: PSYWERX human-factors studies could adapt the multimodal recording workflow to compare attention with task execution in consented training, while explicitly checking synchronization and construct validity. Transfer beyond driving remains untested.
items.streamTitle: Naturalistic driving dataset aligns gaze, physiology and observed actions
items.streamSummary: A public naturalistic driving dataset combines visual attention, physiological measures and vehicle actions, with documented synchronization limitations. It enables research rather than proving intervention effects.
items.attribution: Sanchez-Mateo, Tapia, Lira-Delcore et al. — Scientific Data (data descriptor; November 23, 2026)
